Subject: Post-call notes: capacity, latency targets, and next steps

Thanks for the call this morning — good to meet the team. I wanted to capture the high-level pain, goals, and an initial ask so we’re all aligned before the technical deep-dive later this week.

Pain points we discussed:
- Unpredictable 99th percentile latency during morning batch jobs and peak personalization windows (current 99p ~450ms, spikes to 900ms).
- Token-cost sensitivity: we run many short prompts (~20–60 tokens) with high qps; cost per inference matters.
- Compliance: we need SOC2 evidence, audit logs, and a VPC/private deployment option.

Goals / targets:
- Production SLO: 99th percentile inference latency <= 120ms for short (<=64-token) requests.
- Sustained throughput target: 300 QPS with headroom for 2x burst for marketing spikes.
- Model: Llama3-based family preferred; looking at an 8B quantized candidate but open to alternatives if latency/cost tradeoffs are better.
- Security: VPC deployment, KMS integration, and per-request audit logs retained 90 days.

Immediate asks from MedSys:
1) A clear topology recommendation (hosted + dedicated pools vs private VPC) that meets latency & compliance needs.
2) A rough capacity estimate (GPU type and counts) for 300 QPS at target latency.
3) A proposed mutual action plan and PoC timeline to present to procurement.

Thanks — I’ve copied Alicia from platform to loop in procurement later this week. If anything above is off, correct me and I’ll update.

—Samir

Subject: Technical deep-dive notes & preliminary topology recommendations

Thanks for the call yesterday — below are the technical notes and two topology options we recommend for evaluation during the PoC. I kept the write-up focused on measurable SLOs and ops considerations.

High-level constraints and assumptions (from MedSys deck and call):
- Typical request is short (avg 36 tokens) with bursts tied to marketing/email campaigns.
- Model candidate: Llama3-8B quant (we’ll test 8B int8 and 4-bit quant variants for latency/quality).
- Security: VPC/on-prem option required; HSM/KMS for keys; 90-day audit log retention.

SLOs to validate in PoC:
- P50, P95, P99 latency targets for <=64-token requests; target P99 <= 120ms.
- Sustained QPS: 300; burst handling to 600 QPS with graceful degradation of lower-priority work.

Topology option A — Dedicated GPU pool (Redwood Dedicated) + hosted fallback:
- Primary: Dedicated DGX-style servers (A100 equivalent) reserved for MedSys traffic. Use continuous batching with 5–10ms batching window to keep tail latencies low for short prompts.
- KV/prefix cache colocated in front of model instances to avoid re-computation for repeated prompts.
- Autoscaler: scale by GPU shard count; maintain minimum capacity for steady 300 QPS.
- Estimated PoC footprint: 4 x 80GB GPUs (or equivalent multi-GPU pods) for 300 QPS at target latency with 1.5x headroom. Production (2x) ~8 GPUs.
- Quantization: test 4-bit + group-wise quantization for latency/cost; fall back to int8 if quality drops.
- Security: runs inside customer VPC via Private deployment with KMS integration.

Topology option B — Private VPC deployment (customer-owned network) with Redwood control plane:
- Model served on customer-provisioned instances (on-prem or cloud) managed by Redwood control plane. Allows tight network isolation and compliance.
- Slightly higher cold-start risk; mitigate with warm pools and pre-warming policies for expected bursts.
- Estimated PoC footprint: 3 x 80GB GPUs with aggressive batching and prefix caching; expect slightly higher measured P99 due to network overhead.

Routing & reliability:
- Smart routing policy: route latency-sensitive traffic to Dedicated pool; route background batch jobs to cheaper quantized variants or queued workers.
- Canary rollouts: start with 10% traffic, monitor latency & quality, then 50% -> 100%.

Benchmarks & tests for PoC (deliverables):
1) Synthetic latency sweep for <=64 tokens at 50/150/300/600 QPS measuring P50/P95/P99.
2) Fidelity checks: BLEU/ROUGE-like prompts + human spot-checks for production prompts.
3) Cost model: per-token cost estimates for each topology and quantization point.

Open questions for MedSys (please confirm):
- Do you have a preferred GPU type for on-prem or any cloud constraints?
- What is the procurement timeline and any pre-approved vendor list?

Next steps (owner matrix):
- Karthik: run microbenchmarks and deliver readout by Fri 11/19 (capacity estimate + two configurations).
- Rachel: share mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx with procurement and schedule PoC kickoff.
- Samir/Alicia: provide sample traffic traces (anonymized) and security questionnaire answers.

I’ll attach a short benchmarking checklist after I run the first synthetic tests.

—Karthik Iyer
